title: The Colour out of Space by H. P. Lovecraft

evidence.paraphrase: The events that transformed the region are traced to the arrival of a meteorite.
evidence.quote: It all began, old Ammi said, with the meteorite.

evidence.paraphrase: A rock from space falls to earth and lands near a farm's well.
evidence.quote: the great rock that fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place

evidence.paraphrase: University professors examine and sample the meteorite for laboratory testing.
evidence.quote: The professors tried it with a geologist's hammer and found it was oddly soft. It was, in truth, so soft as to be almost plastic; and they gouged rather than chipped a specimen to take back to the college for testing.

evidence.paraphrase: Spectroscopic testing reveals color bands unlike any known spectrum, prompting talk of new elements.
evidence.quote: when upon heating before the spectroscope it displayed shining bands unlike any known colours of the normal spectrum there was much breathless talk of new elements, bizarre optical properties, and other things which puzzled men of science are wont to say when faced by the unknown

evidence.paraphrase: The scientists systematically test the substance with various reagents and acids, none of which affect it.
evidence.quote: Hot as it was, they tested it in a crucible with all the proper reagents. Water did nothing. Hydrochloric acid was the same. Nitric acid and even aqua regia merely hissed and spattered against its torrid invulnerability.

evidence.paraphrase: The scientists conclude the substance is extraterrestrial and follows laws unlike earthly ones.
evidence.quote: It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.

evidence.paraphrase: The specimen vanishes with a glass beaker, leading scientists to note its affinity for silicon.
evidence.quote: the wise men talked of the strange stone's affinity for silicon

evidence.paraphrase: The farm's fruit grows abnormally large and glossy but becomes inedibly bitter.
evidence.quote: The fruit was growing to phenomenal size and unwonted gloss, and in such abundance that extra barrels were ordered to handle the future crop. But with the ripening came sore disappointment, for of all that gorgeous array of specious lusciousness not one single jot was fit to eat.

evidence.paraphrase: The vegetation on the farm takes on strange colors and forms.
evidence.quote: All the orchard trees blossomed forth in strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth

evidence.paraphrase: The vegetation begins to glow and something phosphorescent stirs in the yard.
evidence.quote: A dim though distinct luminosity seemed to inhere in all the vegetation, grass, leaves, and blossoms alike, while at one moment a detached piece of the phosphorescence appeared to stir furtively in the yard near the barn.

evidence.paraphrase: The livestock undergo grotesque physical decay and death.
evidence.quote: The swine began growing grey and brittle and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles developed singular alterations.

evidence.paraphrase: Mrs. Gardner goes mad, screaming about indescribable things.
evidence.quote: It happened in June, about the anniversary of the meteor's fall, and the poor woman screamed about things in the air which she could not describe.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts with understanding to Ammi's mental state after hearing the tale.
evidence.quote: When he was done I did not wonder that his mind had snapped a trifle, or that the folk of Arkham would not speak much of the blasted heath.

evidence.paraphrase: Laboratory analysis of dust samples links their spectrum to the meteor before the property fades.
evidence.quote: Under the spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange meteor had yielded in the previous year. The property of emitting this spectrum vanished in a month, the dust thereafter consisting mainly of alkaline phosphates and carbonates.

evidence.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysm of unnatural colored substance flung into the sky.
evidence.quote: there burst up from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance; blurring the glance of the few who saw it, and sending forth to the zenith a bombarding cloudburst of such coloured and fantastic fragments as our universe must needs disown

evidence.paraphrase: The colored entity departs by shooting up into the sky through a hole in the clouds.
evidence.quote: Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds before any man could gasp or cry out.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains the entity as a gas-like matter that obeys non-cosmic laws.
evidence.quote: In terms of matter I suppose the thing Ammi described would be called a gas, but this gas obeyed laws that are not of our cosmos.

evidence.paraphrase: The phenomenon is characterized as a color from space beyond known nature.
evidence.quote: It was just a colour out of space	a frightful messenger from unformed realms of infinity beyond all Nature as we know it

evidence.paraphrase: A remnant of the phenomenon is said to be slowly spreading over the land year by year.
evidence.quote: The rustics say the blight creeps an inch a year, so perhaps there is a kind of growth or nourishment even now.

evidence.paraphrase: Ammi is permanently psychologically damaged after recognizing the color's remnant.
evidence.quote: And because Ammi recognized that colour, and knew that this last faint remnant must still lurk down there in the well, he has never been quite right since.

evidence.paraphrase: The substance is compared to known meteoric iron by its magnetism and characteristic figures, yet defies identification.
evidence.quote: It was a metal, though, beyond a doubt. It was magnetic, for one thing; and after its immersion in the acid solvents there seemed to be faint traces of the Widm fnst fntten figures found on meteoric iron.

evidence.paraphrase: The farm is reduced to a barren grey wasteland where nothing grows.
evidence.quote: Five eldritch acres of dusty grey desert remained, nor has anything ever grown there since.
